what_it_shows: Goo-net body-type guide: eight usual body types (sedan, coupe, open car/roadster, station wagon, one-box, minivan, SUV, hatchback/compact) plus kei-car class (660cc, 3.4m x 1.48m x 2m, 4 seats); site nav adds hybrid/EV, commercial, camping car, kei truck/van, bus/truck, welfare vehicle

Rose Bikes: Gravel, Rennrad, MTB, Urban and Trekking, E-Bike; sub-split by use (Adventure/Everyday/Race gravel; Race/Endurance road; XC/Trail/Downhill/Dirt MTB; Urban/Trekking) with e-versions cross-listed under E-Bike
AutoScout24: vehicle tabs Cars, Motorcycles, Caravans, Trucks, Trailers; car body-type quick links Compact, SUV and Pick-up, Transporter, Convertible, Van, Sedan, Station wagon, Coupe
UNECE page hosting Special Resolution No.1 (S.R.1) common definitions of vehicle categories, masses and dimensions

Google Vehicles & Parts: Vehicles = Aircraft, Motor Vehicles (cars/trucks/vans, golf carts, motorcycles and scooters, off-road ATVs/UTVs/go-karts, recreational vehicles, snowmobiles), Watercraft (motor boats, personal watercraft, sailboats, yachts); parts in a separate sibling branch

Wikipedia car body styles (sedan, hatchback, estate, coupe, convertible, roadster, targa, SUV, crossover, MPV, pickup, panel van, ute and others) with regional synonyms; states styles vary by use, market position, location and era

YachtWorld boat-type facet: Power vs Sail, then about 55 power classes (bowrider, center console, trawler, RIB, pontoon, PWC, tender...) and about 28 sail classes (sloop, ketch, catamaran, dinghy...); separate facets for drive type, make, length, price
EU Directive 2013/53/EU: craft 2.5-24 m; design categories A-D by wind force and wave height printed on builder plate; excludes canoes, kayaks, surfboards, racing boats, historic craft

Cycle Trader single Motorcycles-by-Category facet with about 30 values (cruiser, standard, touring, sportbike, custom, dirt bike, scooter, dual sport, trike, moped...) that also lists trailers, PWC, snowmobiles, utility carts and e-bikes in one list

Wikipedia: no universal system for classifying motorcycles; six commonly recognised categories (standard, cruiser, touring, sport, off-road, dual-purpose); scooters, mopeds, minibikes and trikes often excluded; legal and sport-body classes are separate

ISO 4210-2:2023 bicycle safety scope: young adult, city and trekking, mountain, racing (incl. folding) by saddle-height bands; excludes delivery bikes, recumbents, tandems, BMX and competition bikes; smaller ones fall under ISO 8098 or toy rules

FAA aircraft categories (airplane, glider, rotorcraft, lighter-than-air, powered lift, powered parachute, weight-shift control) with classes (SEL, SES, MEL, MES, helicopter, gyroplane, airship, balloon); type = make/model; separate certification categories (normal, utility, experimental, light sport...)
Trade-A-Plane top-level category Single Engine Piston; copy names Cessna, Mooney, Piper as leading makers and the Piper PA-28 Cherokee as a model line with many variants
